chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! Can I perform voluntary prayers in the two Ḥarams and next to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) while I am a Muqassir (one shortening prayers)?' He replied, 'Yes, as much as you are able.'

key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: I shorten (referring to the prayer of Qasr)

ai.seo_question: Can I shorten my voluntary prayers when visiting the shrines of the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual accessibility of the Ahl al-Bayt’s shrines by confirming that travelers may perform voluntary prayers in their entirety or shortened (Qasr) at their discretion. It underscores the flexibility granted to pilgrims in Mecca, Medina, and Karbala, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of these locations as extensions of divine presence. The hadith serves as a practical guide for Ziyarah rituals, affirming that the rules of travel prayer extend seamlessly to devotional acts within these holy precincts.
